heroHeadline: Russia's Victory Day Ceasefire Collapses Within Hours — 850+ Drones, 140+ Attacks; Ukraine Strikes Perm for 3rd Time and Hits Caspian Missile Ship
heroSubtitle: Russia's declared Victory Day ceasefire (midnight May 8 through May 10) collapsed almost immediately. By 7 AM on May 8, Ukraine documented 140+ attacks, 10 assault operations, and 850+ drone strikes — the same combat tempo as any other day. Total daily engagements reached 208: 33 assaults at Pokrovsk, 23 at Huliaipole, 9,113 kamikaze drones deployed, 292 guided aerial bombs. Russia simultaneously threatened a 'massive missile strike on central Kyiv' if Ukraine disrupted the May 9 parade. Ukraine responded by striking the Lukoil-Permnefteorgsintez refinery in Perm for the third time in two weeks (1,500+ km inside Russia), and — for the first time ever — hitting a Russian Karakurt-class missile ship at the Caspian Sea naval base in Kaspiysk, Dagestan (~1,800 km from Ukraine). A Crimea electrical substation and Rostov-on-Don ATC were also struck; 13 Russian airports suspended operations. Russia's 81st Victory Day parade proceeded without tanks, missiles, or armored vehicles for the first time since 2007 — only 2 foreign leaders attended (Fico of Slovakia and Lukashenko of Belarus). ISW confirmed Russia suffered a net loss of 116 sq km in April 2026; Russian daily capture rate has fallen from 9.76 sq km/day (early 2025) to 2.9 sq km/day (early 2026). Total Russian personnel losses: ~1,339,190 — including 1,130 on May 8 alone.
footerNote: Data sourced from UN OHCHR, ISW, CSIS, Ukrainian MoD, US DoD, NATO, IAEA, EU Council, UK MoD, and major news outlets including Reuters, BBC, AP, Al Jazeera, Bloomberg, Kyiv Independent, Euronews, and RBC-Ukraine. Casualty figures are estimates; Russia has never released official figures.
